findings.claim: The isSupported fallback branch is a dead/crashing fallback: when DOMPurify reports unsupported precisely because there is no DOM (SSR, Node test env without jsdom), the else branch dereferences the bare `window` global and throws ReferenceError instead of failing gracefully.
findings.evidence: const purifier = createDOMPurify.isSupported ? createDOMPurify : createDOMPurify(window as unknown as WindowLike); — in any environment where `isSupported` is false due to a missing DOM, `window` is undefined, so the fallback path can never succeed.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the fallback explicitly, e.g. `if (!createDOMPurify.isSupported) { if (typeof window === "undefined") return ""; return createDOMPurify(window as unknown as WindowLike).sanitize(...); }`, or drop the fallback and document that the helper requires a DOM.

findings.claim: The restyled composer/reasoning surfaces now depend on Tailwind 4 theme tokens `--color-surface` and `--color-cyan` whose definitions are not present anywhere in the packet, so if those tokens are not registered in the theme the composer background and reasoning tint silently render transparent/unstyled.
findings.evidence: Hunks replacing `hsl(var(--surface))` with `var(--color-surface)`, `text-[hsl(var(--cyan))]` with `text-[var(--color-cyan)]`, and `bg-[color-mix(in_srgb,var(--color-cyan)_7%,transparent)]`; no theme/CSS file defining these custom properties appears in the diff or is verifiable from the packet.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm (and cite in evidence) that the Tailwind 4 theme defines `--color-surface` and `--color-cyan`, or add the token definitions alongside this change.
